If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
" * Adds 1 to the frequency count for v. *

* If other objects have already been added to this Frequency, v must * be comparable to those that have already been added. *

* * @param v the value to add. * @throws IllegalArgumentException if v is not comparable with previous entries * @throws ClassCastException if v is not Comparable * @deprecated use {@link #addValue(Comparable)} instead "

Title: Diagnosis
Details: 
The failure of the test `testAddNonComparable` arises because the `addValue(Object v)` method in the `Frequency` class currently allows a plain `Object` to be added without verifying if it is `Comparable`. The test expects `ClassCastException` when adding a non-comparable object, but in the current implementation, the first addition of a plain `Object` is allowed, which corrupts the ordering expectations for the frequency table.

Inspecting the implementation of `addValue(Object v)`:
- The code tries to get the count from a frequency map `freqTable` keyed by the object.
- If the object is not comparable to existing entries in the `freqTable` (implemented as a TreeMap, presumably), a `ClassCastException` will be thrown.
- However, this exception handling is only effective when subsequent values are added; the first addition of a plain non-comparable `Object` succeeds because no comparison is needed when adding the first entry.
- This leads to the second addition attempting to compare a non-comparable object against existing keys, triggering an `IllegalArgumentException` (which is thrown wrapping the `ClassCastException`).

From the Javadoc and the current bug report:
- The method is deprecated in favor of `addValue(Comparable)` which enforces type safety.
- The `addValue(Object)` method should only accept comparable objects or internally convert them to comparable types.
- The test expects the method to throw `ClassCastException` immediately when adding a non-comparable object, but this doesn't happen due to missing upfront type checks.

Relevant recent bug reports are unrelated and don't discuss this API or its Comparable enforcement.

The root cause is that `addValue(Object)` does not validate whether the passed object implements `Comparable` before adding it, allowing invalid objects to be inserted as the first key in the frequency map. This breaks the requirement that all objects inserted must be mutually comparable.

The method needs to be fixed by explicitly checking if the passed object is `Comparable` and throwing an exception if not, rather than relying on catching `ClassCastException` later from the TreeMap operations.

Suggested fix locations will revolve around the `Frequency.addValue(Object)` method.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
